title: House prosecutors reject Sara Duterte's 'honest mistake' claim on GenCorp SALN entry
summary: The House prosecution panel has rejected Vice President Sara Duterte's claim that her declaration of GenCorp. Industries, Inc. as one of her business interests in her Statement of Assets, Liabilities…

blocks.text: The House prosecution panel has rejected Vice President Sara Duterte's claim that her declaration of GenCorp. Industries, Inc. as one of her business interests in her Statement of Assets, Liabilities and Net Worth (SALN) could have been an honest mistake, saying she had repeatedly listed the company and its predecessors.

House prosecutor Joel Chua of Manila and prosecution panel adviser Robert Ace Barbers made the remarks in response to Vice Presidential spokesperson Paolo Panelo, who suggested that the inclusion of GenCorp. in Duterte's SALN could have been an honest mistake.

The Vice President is accused of betrayal of public trust and culpable violation of the Constitution over allegations that she accumulated P817 million to P1.5 billion in unexplained wealth through the non-declaration of assets and failure to divest from businesses despite a constitutional prohibition.

“Somebody said the GenCorp. declaration was an honest mistake. But we have to remember, the Vice President declared GenCorp. as her business interest not for one year. She declared it for two consecutive years,” Chua said in an online press conference.
“Prior to GenCorp., she also declared other firms that eventually became GenCorp. as one of her business interests: Davao Bounty, Times Square, among others,” he added.

Chua also questioned the defense's claim that Duterte had no involvement in the companies, citing GenCorp.'s P33-million deal with the Davao City government, which is led by her brother, Mayor Sebastian Duterte.

“That's conflict of interest right there. And their witness said she received P2.1 million return of capital from GenCorp. Given these testimonies from their witnesses appear to testify against the Vice President,” Chua said.
Barbers, meanwhile, said the repeated declaration of the company in Duterte's SALN could not be dismissed as an honest mistake.

“Honest mistake for two consecutive years? If that was made by her staff member, that staff should be fired. Also, inadvertence will not exonerate or exculpate the Vice President from any liability,” Barbers said.
He also argued that Duterte was familiar with the history of the corporations that eventually became GenCorp., indicating that she knew about her investments in the company.

“Kabisadong kabisado ng Vice President ‘yung history… iyong mga prior corporation before the creation of GenCorp. Ibig sabihin, alam na alam niya ‘yung investment niya sa company niyan," Barbers said.
(The Vice President knows the corporation's history. That means she knows her investment in the company.)
"Hindi honest mistake yan. Iyong nagsasabi na ito yung honest mistake, para sa amin tingin namin ito yung palusot,” he added.
"That is not an honest mistake. For us, calling it an honest mistake is just an excuse.)
Defense witnesses have testified that Duterte had no business interests in GenCorp. and its predecessor companies, noting that her name does not appear in their corporate records.
The impeachment trial is set to resume on Thursday, November 19, with the defense continuing to present its evidence.— MCG, GMA News
